newsitem.title: USA: Borden Chemicals conversion plan ended.
newsitem.headline: Borden Chemicals conversion plan ended.

text.p: BCP Management Inc, the general partner of Borden Chemicals and Plastics LP, said Thursday driectors voted to terminate the previously announced plan to convert ownership interests in the partnership into shares of a new corporation, citing U.S. tax law changes.

Under tax laws in effect when the decision was made earlier this year to convert to corporate form, the partnership's exemption from federal income taxes would have expired at the end of 1997, BCP explained. Borden Chemicals and Plastics would have been required to pay corporate tax beginning in 1998.

Through a provision in the tax bill signed into law by President Clinton on August 5, the exemption of publicly traded limited partnerships from federal income taxes is made permanent, and a new 3.5 percent tax is to be levied on gross income beginning January 1, 1998.
Under the new law, publicly traded partnerships retain the ability to convert to corporate form in the future, should they desire.

"Now that the tax law has changed, the benefits to our unitholders of remaining a limited partnership at this time -- even with the 3.5 percent tax -- outweigh those of the proposed conversion," said BCP chief executive Joseph Saggese.

"With the board's action, Borden Chemicals and Plastics will continue to operate as a publicly traded partnership. The partnership will continue its policy of distributing available cash at the end of each quarter to its unitholders, although beginning in 1998, the amount of available cash will be reduced by the new 3.5 percent tax.

Borden Chemicals and Plastics manufactures polyvinyl chloride resins, methanol and derivatives, and nitrogen products at facilities located in Geismar and Addis, La., and Illiopolis, Ill. BCP Management, a subsidiary of Borden Inc, serves as its general partner.
